page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7t.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system is configured with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is moderate, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the average range. However, multi-core performance is comparatively weak, as evidenced by lower-tier results in multi-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth also registers in the lower quartile for both small and large block read/write operations, which limits throughput for memory-intensive operations.

Given these performance characteristics, the ecs.g7t.xlarge is best suited for general-purpose workloads that do not demand high parallel processing power or extreme memory throughput. Appropriate use cases include lightweight web serving, basic text processing, single-threaded applications, and small-scale database operations. The lack of local storage requires external block storage attachment, and the absence of a GPU rules out accelerated computing tasks. The dedicated CPU allocation provides stable execution, but resource-heavy multi-threaded tasks or large-scale data processing will encounter performance bottlenecks.
